newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Outlook for Auckland residential property improves.
newsitem.headline: Outlook for Auckland residential property improves.

text.p: General confidence in the outlook for the Auckland residential property market has improved strongly, according to the latest Massey University quarterly survey, the New Zealand Herald reported on Tuesday.
Overall, a net 59 percent of real estate experts expected an improvement in the next six months.
This was a strong turnaround from a net 53 percent who, in the previous survey, had expected a deterioration in the market over the next half year.
The most confidence was expressed in the outlook for lower and medium priced houses in the North Shore. These were categorised as being valued up to NZ$400,000.
The next most confident grouping was lower valued houses of less than NZ$230,000 in Auckland and less than NZ$190,000 in Waitakere.
The experts were more confident about houses than about apartments, units or sections.
The survey panel was drawn from a broad range of property disciplines, ranging from bankers and real estate agents to property developers and owners.
Generally, sale prices were expected to remain the same or increase over the next three months.
